g.text: Objective: pick the tickers to value, find each one's override file, and load its figures and its dataset region, read and check the override file, then derive the signals the classifier reads.
back to the analyze board

text.tspan: the ticker is asked for
bot analyze TICKER ... or --from-screen
tickers given: those
--from-screen: passed candidates of the latest screener_candidates run (newest created_at), by rank
the command stops before any ticker
no ticker is valued
the ticker is chosen
each ticker of the batch in turn
the override file is settled
--override path (only with exactly one ticker); not a file: exit code two
else config/assumptions/TICKER.yaml when it exists, else none
the ticker is skipped (exit code two)
the batch goes on with the next ticker
the company and its figures are loaded
companies row (name, country, currency, industry_damodaran, ipo_date)
the newest non-restated financials_annual row
oldest-first revenue, net income and earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) histories, empty years dropped
newest prices_daily close
sector pe, ev_sales, op_margin, beta_levered from the newest damodaran_industry row of (industry, region)
valuation currency = currency of that newest non-restated row
the dataset region is set
China, India, Japan: their own dataset region
else from the country's grouping in its newest damodaran_country row
unknown: US
the override file is read and checked
config/assumptions/TICKER.yaml or the --override path, validated whole before the classifier reads the signals
no file: nothing to check; a missing TICKER.yaml or an empty file counts as no file
the signals are derived
net debt, interest coverage, age, founded age and the cyclical sector

g.text: the ticker cannot be valued (exit code 1)
screener_candidates
companies
financials_annual
prices_daily
damodaran_industry
damodaran_country

text.tspan: Comes out:
one loaded company: its newest annual figures and histories, newest close, sector multiples, dataset region, valuation currency, the checked override file or none, and the signals
the ticker is named on the command line
[tickers named, no --from-screen]

g.text: the latest screen lists it as a passed candidate [--from-screen]
the command stops, exit code two [tickers with --from-screen, neither, --override without exactly one ticker, or an --override path that is not a file]
the command stops, exit code 1 [a rate in config/currencies.yaml is out of range]
the command stops, exit code two [--from-screen, and no screen run or no passed candidate]
the override file is the one --override names [exactly one ticker]
the override file is config/assumptions/TICKER.yaml [it exists]
no override file [no --override, no TICKER.yaml]
the ticker is skipped, exit code two [not in companies, or no annual financials]
the company, its newest annual figures, history, close and sector multiples are loaded
the dataset region is its own [China, India, Japan]

text.tspan: the dataset region comes from its country's grouping
[not China, India or Japan; grouping known]

g.text: the dataset region is US [grouping unknown]
the override file is read and checked [a valid file, or none]

text.tspan: the ticker cannot be valued, exit code 1 [the override file is not valid YAML, not a mapping, has an unknown key or a value that is not a finite number, or its story file is inconsistent]
the file is validated whole before the signals are derived
a founded_year that is not a whole year from 1600 to this year also refuses the file
net debt, interest coverage, age, founded age and the cyclical sector are derived
net debt = total debt − cash, a missing term counts as 0
interest coverage = EBIT ÷ interest expense, empty when EBIT is missing, or interest expense is 0 or missing
age = whole years since ipo_date
founded age = this year − founded_year of the override file, unknown without it
cyclical sector = industry_damodaran in the cyclical list (exact match)

g.text: passed candidates of the latest run, by rank
company row
annual rows
newest close
sector multiples
country grouping
the loaded company goes on to the story type [always]
